title: 4GE1-style exam questions: Causes of river flooding, prediction and prevention (1.3)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 56 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 56: Causes of river flooding, prediction and prevention (1.3). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Assess the effectiveness of hard and soft engineering in reducing flood risk.' Plan, then write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Hard: immediate, strong protection but costly and can shift risk; soft: cheaper, sustainable but slower and needs land; examples (Jubilee River); judgement on which is more effective and where
questions.model: Teacher plans: intro; P1 hard engineering strengths and limits with an example; P2 soft engineering strengths and limits; P3 combined approaches; conclusion with a justified judgement.

questions.q: Suggest why flood risk may increase in the future.
questions.a: Climate change brings heavier rainfall (1); more building on flood plains (1); more impermeable surfaces (1)

questions.q: Why is flood plain zoning a sustainable strategy?
questions.a: It keeps homes off high-risk land (1), so less damage and no costly defences (1)

questions.q: Explain how urbanisation increases flood risk.
questions.a: Concrete and tarmac are impermeable (1), so less infiltration and more surface runoff (1); drains carry water quickly to the river, raising peak discharge (1)
questions.model: Surface change: impermeable concrete. Process change: less infiltration, more runoff. River change: water arrives faster, so a higher peak.

questions.q: State two ways floods are predicted.
questions.a: Two of: weather forecasts and radar, rain gauges, river level gauges, computer models

questions.q: Give one disadvantage of hard engineering.
questions.a: For example: expensive, or can increase flooding downstream

questions.q: Big question: is it better to stop rivers flooding or to stop people living where they flood?
questions.a: A balanced judgement: combine defences where many people live with zoning and soft engineering elsewhere
